leftEvidence.title: One heart and an everlasting covenant

points.label: Covenant setting
points.left: Covenant language is placed beside inward change, enduring good, return, and renewed settlement.
points.right: The passage names internalized law, knowing Yahweh, forgiveness, and remembered sin no more as features of the promised covenant.

points.label: Parties, action, or promise
points.left: Judah · gathered people · Land · Scattered → gathered · one heart and way · Everlasting covenant · not turn from doing good
points.right: Israel · Judah · Law written on heart · I will be their God · they my people · forgiveness · Broken former covenant → new covenant

payload.posture: Adjacent Jeremiah promises join inward change, restored relationship, forgiveness, gathering, and enduring covenant.

rightEvidence.title: A new covenant after a broken one

payload.tension: The two sources materially share covenant language or memory, while their parties, setting, action, or literary purpose remain distinct.
payload.title: One heart and one way / law written on the heart
